case_title: Raju & Anr. v. State of Haryana
accused_victim_relationship: Prior dispute: the deceased allegedly misbehaved with women at a marriage ceremony, leading to the later assault
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony; medical evidence (post-mortem and injuries)
aggravating_circumstances: Victim was chased, surrounded and held before being fatally stabbed with knives
mitigating_circumstances: Provocation from the deceased's misbehaviour toward women at a marriage ceremony; appellants were unarmed
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC; sentenced to life imprisonment and fine of Rs.5,000 each (default three years RI)
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC confirmed
offence_finally_established: IPC s.304 Part I r/w s.34
neutral_facts: The victim was reportedly intoxicated at a marriage ceremony where he misbehaved towards women who were singing and participating in festivities. Later that evening, around 10.30 p.m., as the victim was returning home after watching a film, a group of four men attacked him with fists near the gate of a government livestock farm. The victim ran toward his home but was chased and surrounded near another house. A witness, the victim's brother, stated he was nearby and saw the incident. Two of the men carried knives, while the other two were empty-handed. The brother's account was that two of the men held the victim while the other two stabbed him, one blow to the left chest and another to the waist. On an alarm being raised, the group fled. The victim was taken toward hospital but died on the way. A post-mortem examination found multiple ante-mortem injuries sufficient to cause death, with the cause given as shock and haemorrhage. The first information report was lodged by the brother, who identified the men who held and stabbed the victim. An eyewitness other than the brother also gave evidence of the incident, and the injuries on the victim's body were consistent with that account.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from shock and haemorrhage due to multiple ante-mortem injuries, including knife wounds to the chest and waist
number_of_offences: 1 charged (IPC s.302 r/w s.34); 0 finally upheld as charged (altered to s.304 Part I r/w s.34)
premeditation_planning: Not found; no common intention to murder established, and the assault was an immediate response to the earlier incident
motive: Response to the deceased's misbehaviour toward women at a marriage ceremony, with intention to preserve their honour and dignity
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness evidence of PW.5 (complainant) and PW.7, corroborated by injuries on the victim's body; post-mortem evidence of PW.8
witness_credibility: Eyewitness evidence of PW.5 and PW.7 was corroborated by the injuries, but the court held this did not by itself establish common intention as to the appellants
trial_duration: offence: 31 March 1994; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 30 October 2007; Supreme Court: 10 February 2010
legal_representation: Accused: Rishi Malhotra (Advocate). State of Haryana: Manjit Singh and Kamal Mohan Gupta (Advocates)
investigation_status: FIR lodged by the complainant; post-mortem conducted on 1 April 1994; trial completed before the trial court
procedural_irregularity: Appellant No.1 was found to be a juvenile at the time of the offence, so his case was referred to the Juvenile Justice Board rather than decided as an adult
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC, life imprisonment. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction confirmed. Supreme Court: appeal allowed in part, conviction altered to s.304 Part I r/w s.34 IPC
prosecution_argument: Appellant No.2 was part of the group that chased the victim and held him while the co-accused stabbed him, showing common motive and common intention; conviction under s.302 r/w s.34 should be upheld
defence_argument: No prior meeting of minds or common intention to kill; appellants did not know the co-accused carried knives and only intended to teach the victim a lesson; s.302 r/w s.34 wrongly applied; juvenility of Appellant No.1 to be considered under the Juvenile Justice Act
legal_principle_applied: Liability under s.34 requires common intention; absent that, the role attributed attracts s.304 Part I rather than s.302 r/w s.34
precedent_relied_upon: V. Sreedharan vs. State of Kerala, 1992 Supp (3) SCC 21 (relied on); Hari Ram vs. State of Rajasthan and Anr., 2009 (6) SCALE 695 (referred to)
judicial_mitigating_factors: Provocation from the deceased's intoxicated misbehaviour toward women at a marriage ceremony; role limited to chasing and holding the victim, with no common intention to kill
other_sentence_order: Appellant No.1's records to be transmitted to the Juvenile Justice Board; Appellant No.2 entitled to set-off of detention under s.428 Cr.P.C.; fine default of 15 days RI for Appellant No.2
